title: feat(crypto)!: BLS12-381 v3 keysets
body:
## Summary

Adds support for **v3 keysets** (keyset id prefix `02`), which use BLS12-381 instead of secp256k1 for BDHKE. Wire-compatible with [Nutshell PR #999](https://github.com/cashubtc/nutshell/pull/999) — a v3 cashu-ts wallet redeems against a v3 Nutshell mint without ambiguity.

What changes for v3 proofs:

- **Multiplicative blinding** on BLS12-381 G1 (`B_ = Y · r`, `C_ = B_ · a`, `C = C_ · r⁻¹`).
- **DLEQ is gone.** A single pairing equality `e(C, G2_gen) == e(Y, K2)` replaces it (`K2` is the mint pubkey in G2). One pairing call instead of ~4 scalar mults + hash + wire bytes per proof.
- **Batch verification** via a single multi-pairing wired into the receive path (`verifyProofsForReceive`); typical mixed-denomination tokens get one pairing call total.

v0 (legacy base64), v1 (`00…`), v2 (`01…`) keysets are untouched and continue to work. The DLEQ code paths remain in service of those keysets.

## Breaking change

`Wallet.checkProofsStates` now requires both `id` and `secret` on every input (previously only `secret`). The `id` selects the hash-to-curve variant for the NUT-07 lookup point `Y` — secp256k1 for v0/v1/v2, BLS12-381 G1 for v3. Without it, v3 proofs silently miscompute `Y` and the state check returns nothing. Callers passing full `Proof` objects are unaffected. See [migration-5.0.0.md](./migration-5.0.0.md).

## Highlights

- New `src/crypto/bls.ts` — BLS12-381 primitives (blind, unblind, sign, single + batch verify, hash-to-curve, deterministic batch weights via Fiat-Shamir).
- `CurvePoint` tagged union — point types widen across `OutputData`, `BlindedMessage`, `BlindedSignature`, mint-pubkey parsing to cover both curves cleanly.
- NUT-13 HMAC derivation reduces mod the BLS scalar field for v3; secp256k1 path unchanged.
- Mint-side v3 keyset generation matches Nutshell `derive_keys_v3` (hardened path + sha256-of-bip32 before Fr reduction).
- Wallet receive path batches v3 verification; mixed v1/v2/v3 tokens split correctly between DLEQ and pairing.
- BAT (NUT-22 auth) verification accepts v3 auth keysets.
- Integration tests wired against a v3 Nutshell mint via `examples/auth_mint/docker-compose-nutshell.yml`.

## Test plan

- [x] Full unit suite (4345 tests) passes in node + chromium + firefox + webkit
- [x] BLS deterministic vector (`secret="test_message"`, r=3, a=2) reproduces `B_`, `C_`, `C` byte-for-byte vs Nutshell
- [x] Pairing equality test against locked Nutshell vectors
- [x] Batch verify forgery defence: `(C₁, secret₁), (C − C₁, secret₂)` aggregation attack rejected
- [x] Mixed v1/v2/v3 receive token: each subset verified by its appropriate path; tampered proof in either subset surfaces the offender
- [x] NUT-13 v3 vector cross-checked against Nutshell `_derive_secret_hmac_sha256` at counter where the raw HMAC exceeds `BLS_FR_ORDER` (so the mod-Fr branch is exercised)
- [x] Round-trip: v3 token `getEncodedToken` → `getDecodedToken` preserves the `02…` id
- [x] `checkProofsStates` migration: v3 proofs now match against the mint's G1 `Y` (previously silently empty)
- [x] Integration suite against a live v3 Nutshell mint (`make integration-nutshell-bls`) — requires running mint, smoke-tested locally
- [x] Cross-check v3 mint key seed → keys parity with Nutshell `derive_keys_v3`: byte-for-byte locked vector in `test/crypto/NUT01.test.ts` (`mnemonic='TEST_PRIVATE_KEY'`, `path m/0'/0'/0'`, `amounts [1,2,4,8]`, `unit 'sat'`)

## References

- [Nutshell PR #999](https://github.com/cashubtc/nutshell/pull/999) — reference implementation

title: feat: add onchain mint/melt support
body:
Adds onchain (Bitcoin) mint and melt support per [NUT-30](https://github.com/cashubtc/nuts/pull/365).

## What's new

### Onchain minting
- `Wallet.createMintQuoteOnchain(pubkey)` / `Mint.createMintQuoteOnchain(...)`, request a pubkey-locked onchain mint quote
- `Wallet.checkMintQuoteOnchain(quote)` / `Mint.checkMintQuoteOnchain(...)`
- `Wallet.mintProofsOnchain(amount, quote, privkey, ...)` / `Mint.mintOnchain(...)`
- `WalletOps.mintOnchain(amount, quote)` builder

Onchain mint quotes are **locked to a public key**. The quote response carries `amount_paid` and `amount_issued` so callers can mint incrementally as on-chain funds confirm; a guard prevents over-minting a partially-paid quote.

### Onchain melting
- `Wallet.createMeltQuoteOnchain(address, amount)` / `Mint.createMeltQuoteOnchain(...)`
- `Wallet.checkMeltQuoteOnchain(quote)` / `Mint.checkMeltQuoteOnchain(...)`
- `Wallet.meltProofsOnchain(quote, proofs, estimatedBlocks, ...)` / `Mint.meltOnchain(...)`
- `WalletOps.meltOnchain(quote, proofs)` -> `MeltOnchainBuilder` (`.estimatedBlocks()`, `.keyset()`, `.privkey()`, `.run()`)

A melt quote returns a **single quote with multiple `fee_options`** (each pairing a `fee_reserve` with `estimated_blocks`); the fee tier is selected at execution time. The response exposes `selected_estimated_blocks` and `outpoint` once broadcast. NUT-08 change is supported on onchain melt.

### Supporting changes
- `MintMethod` extended with `'onchain'`; `MintBuilder`/`MintQuoteFor` updated accordingly
- New types: `MintQuoteOnchain{Request,Response}`, `MeltQuoteOnchain{Request,Response}`, `MeltQuoteOnchainFeeOption` (`src/model/types/NUT30.ts`)
- `completeMelt` now takes a `CompleteMeltOptions` object (`preferAsync`, `extraPayload`); the positional `preferAsync` overload is kept and `@deprecated`
- `MeltProofsResponse` now exposes `outputData`, so deferred NUT-08 change can be recovered
- `prepareMelt` config widened to `PrepareMeltConfig` (adds `nut08Change`)
- `SwapMethod.options` gains `confirmations`
- Onchain methods carry an `@experimental` tag pending NUT-30 finalization

### Examples & docs
- New interactive `examples/onchain_example.ts` (listed in `examples/README.md`)

### Tests
Unit and node integration coverage for onchain mint/melt across `Mint`, `Wallet`, and `WalletOps`.
